This page helps you spot repeated or similar chart lettering and check whether charts contain different parts of an alphabet. Similarity is a clue for comparing pages; it does not prove that two charts belong to the same historical font.

<p id="similarity-page-status" class="font-status" role="status" aria-live="polite">Loading chart comparisons…</p>

<div id="similarity-overview" class="font-research-metrics" aria-label="Comparison summary"></div>

<section aria-labelledby="close-pages-heading">
<h2 id="close-pages-heading">Compare similar charts</h2>
<p>Choose a pair to see every charted glyph. Letters present on both charts appear larger; glyphs unique to one chart remain visible at a smaller size. Each glyph keeps its chart’s original Org font.</p>
<label for="similar-chart-pair">Chart pair</label>
<select id="similar-chart-pair" class="form-select"></select>
<div id="selected-pair-note" class="font-source-note"></div>
<div id="selected-pair-cloud" class="font-glyph-cloud" aria-live="polite"></div>
</section>

<section aria-labelledby="coverage-heading">
<h2 id="coverage-heading">What is on each chart?</h2>
<p>Open a source group to see each chart’s recorded letters and numbers. Different letter ranges may be useful clues when checking for partial alphabets, but do not confirm that pages were meant to be joined.</p>
<div id="chart-coverage"></div>
</section>

<section aria-labelledby="exact-repeats-heading">
<h2 id="exact-repeats-heading">Repeated glyphs</h2>
<p>Some individual letters have exactly the same filled-cell shape on more than one chart. This supports comparing those letters, but does not mean the whole charts are duplicates.</p>
<div id="exact-repeats"></div>
</section>

<details class="font-method-details">
<summary>How the comparison works</summary>
<p>Each glyph is cropped to its filled cells, scaled proportionally to fit a centered 18 × 18 binary grid, then compared by Jaccard overlap. Page scores average shared letter shapes; case variants count as the same label. The close-match screen uses a mean score of 0.85 or above across at least three shared letters. This is an exploratory review aid, not a validated duplicate-font threshold.</p>
<p>The measure ignores color, stitch texture, spacing, page layout, manuscript dating, and reader perception. Chart coverage retains the recorded case. The [metric data](fonts/similarity-metrics.json) and [font-generation README](fonts/README.md) document the full method and limits.</p>
</details>
